from m5.util import addToPath

m5.util.addToPath("../../")

from common import ObjectList, MemConfig
from common.cores.arm import O3_ARM_v7a
import devices
from devices import L1I, L1D, L2, SimpleSeSystem, ArmCpuCluster

# ArmBareMetalWorkload is exported via m5.objects automatically
# BareMetalLoader is auto-registered when C++ code is imported
# No explicit import needed - gem5's Python binding exports it


def _build_parser() -> argparse.ArgumentParser:
    p = argparse.ArgumentParser(
        description="Run an ARM64 bare-metal static ELF in gem5 SE mode."
    )
    p.add_argument("binary", type=Path, help="Path to the ARM64 ELF to run.")
    p.add_argument("--cpu", choices=["atomic", "timing", "o3", "minor"], default="atomic")
    p.add_argument("--cpu-freq", default="2.6GHz")
    p.add_argument("--num-cores", type=int, default=1)
    p.add_argument("--mem-size", default="4GiB")
    p.add_argument("--mem-channels", type=int, default=1)
    p.add_argument("--mem-type", default="DDR3_1600_8x8")
    p.add_argument("--mem-ranks", type=int, default=None)
    p.add_argument("--max-ticks", type=int, default=None)
    p.add_argument(
        "-P", "--param", action="append", default=[],
        help="Set SimObject params.",
    )
    return p


def _cpu_type_info(cpu_name: str):
    lut = {
        "atomic": (AtomicSimpleCPU, None, None, None),
        "timing": (TimingSimpleCPU, L1I, L1D, L2),
        "o3": (O3_ARM_v7a.O3_ARM_v7a_3, L1I, L1D, L2),
        "minor": (MinorCPU, L1I, L1D, L2),
    }
    return lut[cpu_name]


def main() -> None:
    args = _build_parser().parse_args()

    cpu_cls, l1i_cls, l1d_cls, l2_cls = _cpu_type_info(args.cpu)
    mem_mode = cpu_cls.memory_mode()
    want_caches = mem_mode == "timing"

    # System
    system = SimpleSeSystem(mem_mode=mem_mode)

    # CPU cluster
    system.cpu_cluster = ArmCpuCluster(
        system,
        args.num_cores,
        args.cpu_freq,
        "1.2V",
        cpu_cls, l1i_cls, l1d_cls, l2_cls,
    )
    system.addCaches(want_caches, last_cache_level=2)

    system.mem_ranges = [AddrRange(start=0, size=args.mem_size)]

    MemConfig.config_mem(args, system)
    system.connect()

    # Bare-metal workload
    binary_path = str(args.binary.resolve())

    # Bare-metal workload — auto-selects ArmBareMetalProcess via BareMetalLoader
    system.workload = ArmBareMetalWorkload()

    # Create single process and assign to all CPUs
    process = Process()
    process.executable = binary_path
    process.cmd = [binary_path]

    # Assign same process to each CPU (ArmCpuCluster already handles threading)
    for cpu in system.cpu_cluster.cpus:
        cpu.workload = process

    root = Root(full_system=False)
    root.system = system
    root.apply_config(args.param)

    m5.instantiate()

    # BareMetalWorkload::initState() (C++) sets PC to ELF entry and SP to 0x80010000
    # No manual PC/SP setup needed — the C++ layer handles it.
    pass

    print(
        f"Running {args.binary} on {args.cpu} CPU ({mem_mode} mode)...",
        file=sys.stderr,
    )

    exit_event = m5.simulate(args.max_ticks or 10**12)

    print(
        f"Exited @ tick {m5.curTick()} "
        f"because {exit_event.getCause()} ({exit_event.getCode()})",
        file=sys.stderr,
    )


if __name__ == "__m5_main__":
    main()

    type = "ArmEmuLinux"
    cxx_header = "arch/arm/linux/se_workload.hh"
    cxx_class = "gem5::ArmISA::EmuLinux"

    @classmethod
    def _is_compatible_with(cls, obj):
        return obj.get_arch() in (
            "arm64",
            "arm",
            "thumb",
        ) and obj.get_op_sys() in ("linux", "unknown")


class ArmEmuFreebsd(ArmSEWorkload):
    type = "ArmEmuFreebsd"
    cxx_header = "arch/arm/freebsd/se_workload.hh"
    cxx_class = "gem5::ArmISA::EmuFreebsd"

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Materialize vault assembly snippets into runnable ARM64 C sources."""

from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import json
from pathlib import Path
from typing import Any, Dict, Iterable, List, Mapping, Optional

from sdc_vault import SDCVault


REPO_ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parent
DEFAULT_OUTPUT_ROOT = REPO_ROOT / "artifacts" / "materialized"


def _escape_c_string(value: str) -> str:
    return value.replace("\\", "\\\\").replace('"', '\\"')


def _asm_block(lines: Iterable[str]) -> str:
    return "\n".join(f'"{_escape_c_string(line)}\\n"' for line in lines if line.strip())


def render_materialized_source(asm_content: str, testcase_key: str) -> str:
    asm_lines = [line.rstrip() for line in asm_content.splitlines() if line.strip()]
    if not asm_lines:
        asm_lines = ["nop"]

        ".text",
        ".align 4",

def create(args):
    """Create and configure the system object."""

    cpu_class = cpu_types[args.cpu][0]
    mem_mode = cpu_class.memory_mode()
    # Only simulate caches when using a timing CPU (e.g., the HPI model)
    want_caches = True if mem_mode == "timing" else False

    system = devices.SimpleSeSystem(
        mem_mode=mem_mode,
    )

    # Add CPUs to the system. A cluster of CPUs typically have
    # private L1 caches and a shared L2 cache.
    system.cpu_cluster = devices.ArmCpuCluster(
        system,
        args.num_cores,
        args.cpu_freq,
        "1.2V",
        *cpu_types[args.cpu],
        tarmac_gen=args.tarmac_gen,
        tarmac_dest=args.tarmac_dest,

    # Create a cache hierarchy for the cluster. We are assuming that
    # clusters have core-private L1 caches and an L2 that's shared

    system.addCaches(want_caches, last_cache_level=2)

# Copyright 2026
# Licensed under the Apache License, Version 2.0

"""Minimal bare-metal ARM64 SE runner for SDC power analysis via gem5."""

from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import sys
from pathlib import Path

import m5
from m5.objects import *
from m5.util import addToPath

m5.util.addToPath("../../")

from common import ObjectList, MemConfig
from common.cores.arm import O3_ARM_v7a
import devices
from devices import L1I, L1D, L2, SimpleSeSystem, ArmCpuCluster

# ArmBareMetalWorkload is exported via m5.objects automatically
# BareMetalLoader is auto-registered when C++ code is imported
# No explicit import needed - gem5's Python binding exports it


def _build_parser() -> argparse.ArgumentParser:
    p = argparse.ArgumentParser(
        description="Run an ARM64 bare-metal static ELF in gem5 SE mode."
    )
    p.add_argument("binary", type=Path, help="Path to the ARM64 ELF to run.")
    p.add_argument("--cpu", choices=["atomic", "timing", "o3", "minor"], default="atomic")
    p.add_argument("--cpu-freq", default="2.6GHz")
    p.add_argument("--num-cores", type=int, default=1)
    p.add_argument("--mem-size", default="4GiB")
    p.add_argument("--mem-channels", type=int, default=1)
    p.add_argument("--mem-type", default="DDR3_1600_8x8")
    p.add_argument("--mem-ranks", type=int, default=None)
    p.add_argument("--max-ticks", type=int, default=None)
    p.add_argument(
        "-P", "--param", action="append", default=[],
        help="Set SimObject params.",
    )
    return p


def _cpu_type_info(cpu_name: str):
    lut = {
        "atomic": (AtomicSimpleCPU, None, None, None),
        "timing": (TimingSimpleCPU, L1I, L1D, L2),
        "o3": (O3_ARM_v7a.O3_ARM_v7a_3, L1I, L1D, L2),
        "minor": (MinorCPU, L1I, L1D, L2),
    }
    return lut[cpu_name]


def main() -> None:
    args = _build_parser().parse_args()

    cpu_cls, l1i_cls, l1d_cls, l2_cls = _cpu_type_info(args.cpu)
    mem_mode = cpu_cls.memory_mode()
    want_caches = mem_mode == "timing"

    # System
    system = SimpleSeSystem(mem_mode=mem_mode)

    # CPU cluster
    system.cpu_cluster = ArmCpuCluster(
        system,
        args.num_cores,
        args.cpu_freq,
        "1.2V",
        cpu_cls, l1i_cls, l1d_cls, l2_cls,
    )
    system.addCaches(want_caches, last_cache_level=2)

    system.mem_ranges = [AddrRange(start=0, size=args.mem_size)]

    MemConfig.config_mem(args, system)
    system.connect()

    # Bare-metal workload
    binary_path = str(args.binary.resolve())

    # Let gem5 auto-detect workload type based on ELF OS field
    # BareMetalLoader in C++ will be matched for UnknownOpSys ARM64 binaries
    system.workload = SEWorkload.init_compatible(binary_path)

    # Create single process and assign to all CPUs
    process = Process()
    process.executable = binary_path
    process.cmd = [binary_path]

    # Assign same process to each CPU (ArmCpuCluster already handles threading)
    for cpu in system.cpu_cluster.cpus:
        cpu.workload = process

    root = Root(full_system=False)
    root.system = system
    root.apply_config(args.param)

    m5.instantiate()

    # BareMetalWorkload::initState() (C++) sets PC to ELF entry and SP to 0x80010000
    # No manual PC/SP setup needed — the C++ layer handles it.
    pass

    print(
        f"Running {args.binary} on {args.cpu} CPU ({mem_mode} mode)...",
        file=sys.stderr,
    )

    exit_event = m5.simulate(args.max_ticks or 10**12)

    print(
        f"Exited @ tick {m5.curTick()} "
        f"because {exit_event.getCause()} ({exit_event.getCode()})",
        file=sys.stderr,
    )


if __name__ == "__m5_main__":
    main()

def _build_parser() -> argparse.ArgumentParser:
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(
        description="Materialize vault assembly entries into ARM64 C sources."
    )
    parser.add_argument("--db", type=Path, required=True, help="Vault database path.")
    parser.add_argument(
        "--testcase-key",
        action="append",
        default=[],
        help="Specific testcase key to materialize. Repeat as needed.",
    )
    parser.add_argument(
        "--limit",
        type=int,
        default=0,
        help="If no testcase key is provided, materialize up to this many pending entries.",
    )
    parser.add_argument(
        "--output-root",
        type=Path,
        default=DEFAULT_OUTPUT_ROOT,
        help="Directory for generated C files.",
    )
    return parser


def main() -> int:
    args = _build_parser().parse_args()
    with SDCVault(args.db) as vault:
        testcase_keys = list(args.testcase_key)
        if not testcase_keys:
            pending = vault.fetch_top_k_risky(args.limit or 10)
            testcase_keys = [str(row["testcase_key"]) for row in pending]

        materialized = [
            str(materialize_testcase(vault, testcase_key, output_root=args.output_root))
            for testcase_key in testcase_keys
        ]

    payload = {
        "count": len(materialized),
        "sources": materialized,
    }
    print(json.dumps(payload, indent=2, ensure_ascii=False))
    return 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    raise SystemExit(main())

    return "\n".join(f'"{_escape_c_string(line)}\\n"' for line in lines if line.strip())


def render_materialized_source(asm_content: str, testcase_key: str) -> str:

The ARM64 bare-metal SE workload execution fails with "unknown instruction (inst 0xf9000fe0)" panic in gem5.

## Phase 2：LLM 增强的智能变异生成（后续）

### Step A: LLM 变异生成器

**目标**：借助 LLM 推理能力，实现更精准的 SDC 检测指令流生成。

**新建文件**：`microprobe/targets/arm64/policies/llm_guided_policy.py`

**核心功能**：
1. **LLM Prompt 生成器**：基于当前功耗/覆盖率反馈构建变异提示
2. **变异算子库**：支持多种变异策略
3. **指令流生成**：基于 LLM 推理生成高风险指令序列

**变异算子类型**：
- `insert`：在指令序列中插入新指令
- `delete`：删除现有指令
- `replace`：替换指令操作码或操作数
- `IMMUTATE`：改变立即数值（增加位翻转风险）
- `STRIDE mutate`：改变内存访问步长（触发 Cache 驱逐）
- `REG mutate`：改变寄存器分配（改变依赖图）
- `REORDER`：指令重排（改变流水线调度）
- `DUPLICATE`：复制高风险指令增加执行频率
- `CROSSOVER`：两个指令序列交换子序列

### Step B: 概率上下文文法（PCFG）生成器

**目标**：基于概率分布的指令序列生成。

**核心功能**：
- 从 Vault 提取真实指令序列，学习 N-gram 概率分布
- 生成符合 ARM64 ISA 语法的指令序列
- 优先采样高功耗/高风险指令组合

### Step C: 模板生成器

**目标**：基于预定义模板生成指令序列。

**核心功能**：
- 定义常见 SDC 敏感模式模板（如 FMA 链、LDP/STP 交叉）
- 基于模板参数化生成变体
- 支持模板组合和嵌套

### Step D: 遗传算法（GA）优化器

**目标**：基于功耗/覆盖率/风险评分的种群优化。

**新建文件**：`microprobe/src/microprobe/driver/sdc_genetic_driver.py`

**核心功能**：
- **Fitness 函数**：`ACE * IBR * (1 / (power + 1)) * risk_score`
- **选择算子**：锦标赛选择、轮盘赌选择
- **交叉算子**：单点交叉、均匀交叉、模拟二进制交叉（SBX）
- **变异算子**：高斯变异、多项式变异
- **精英保留**：保留 Top-K 最优个体

### Step E: LLM 覆盖率评估器

**目标**：借助 LLM 实现更全面的覆盖率评估。

**新建文件**：`microprobe/src/microprobe/passes/sdc_analysis/llm_coverage_pass.py`

**核心功能**：
- 调用 LLM 分析指令依赖图
- 评估数据 Hazard（RAW、WAR、WAW）
- 评估结构 Hazard（执行单元冲突）
- 评估控制流复杂度
- 生成综合覆盖率评分

### Step F: LLM Prompt 生成

**目标**：构建高效的 LLM 生成提示。

**提示工程要点**：
1. 包含 ACE/IBR/内存压力/risk_score 等评分上下文
2. 指定目标架构（ARM64 Kunpeng920 微架构）
3. 指定约束条件（指令兼容性、寄存器分配）
4. 要求生成特定模式的指令序列

**示例提示**：
```
You are a CPU microarchitecture expert specializing in ARM64 SDC detection.
Generate an 8-instruction sequence that maximizes:
- ACE (Architectural Criticality Estimator): high register lifetime
- IBR (Instruction Bit Reach): wide data path usage (128-bit SIMD)
- Memory pressure: cache eviction patterns

Context:
- Power: 1.234W, Variance: 0.567
- ACE: 0.876, IBR: 0.654, Risk: 0.789
- Previous sequences failed due to: register dependency chain too short

Constraints:
- Use FMADD, FMLA, LDP, STP instructions only
- Avoid X16, X17 (temporary registers)
- Memory stride >= 8192 for cache pressure
- Total instruction count: 8

Output: ARM64 assembly sequence (one instruction per line)
```

# Copyright 2026
# Licensed under the Apache License, Version 2.0

"""ARM64 SDC fuzzing policy tuned for Kunpeng920-style stress patterns."""

from __future__ import absolute_import, print_function

import microprobe.code
import microprobe.passes.address
import microprobe.passes.branch
import microprobe.passes.initialization
import microprobe.passes.instruction
import microprobe.passes.memory
import microprobe.passes.register
import microprobe.passes.structure
import microprobe.passes.sdc_analysis
from microprobe.exceptions import MicroprobePolicyError
from microprobe.utils.logger import get_logger
from microprobe.utils.misc import RND, RNDINT

__all__ = [
    "NAME",
    "DESCRIPTION",
    "SUPPORTED_TARGETS",
    "SDCSensitiveAnalyzer",
    "policy",
]

NAME = "sdc_fuzzing"
DESCRIPTION = "Static-score-first SDC fuzzing policy for ARM64"
SUPPORTED_TARGETS = ["all"]

LOG = get_logger(__name__)


def _target_looks_like_arm64(target):
    registers = getattr(target, "registers", {})
    return all(reg in registers for reg in ["X0", "SP", "V0", "LR"])


class SDCSensitiveAnalyzer(object):
    """Pick ARM64 instructions that are more likely to expose silent faults."""

    _FMA_MNEMONICS = {"FMADD", "FMSUB", "FNMADD", "FNMSUB"}
    _PAIR_MEMORY_MNEMONICS = {"LDP", "STP"}
    # LSE atomics (CASAL, CASA, CASL, etc.) require separate handling and
    # are excluded here to keep the toolchain compatible with aarch64-elf
    # toolchains that lack LSE support.
    _LSE_PREFIXES = ()

    def __init__(self, target):
        self._target = target

    def collect(self):
        instructions = list(self._target.isa.instructions.values())
        fma = []
        pair_memory = []
        lse = []
        for instr in instructions:
            mnemonic = instr.mnemonic.upper()
            if mnemonic in self._FMA_MNEMONICS:
                fma.append(instr)
                continue
            if (
                mnemonic in self._PAIR_MEMORY_MNEMONICS
                and instr.name.endswith("_X_V0")
            ):
                pair_memory.append(instr)
                continue
            if any(mnemonic.startswith(prefix) for prefix in self._LSE_PREFIXES):
                lse.append(instr)

        for bucket in [fma, pair_memory, lse]:
            bucket.sort(key=lambda instr: instr.name)

        sensitive = []
        max_len = max(len(fma), len(pair_memory), len(lse), 1)
        for idx in range(max_len):
            if idx < len(fma):
                sensitive.append(fma[idx])
            if idx < len(pair_memory):
                sensitive.append(pair_memory[idx])
            if idx < len(lse):
                sensitive.append(lse[idx])

        return sensitive

    def default_sequence(self, limit=8):
        sensitive = self.collect()
        if not sensitive:
            raise MicroprobePolicyError(
                "No ARM64 SDC-sensitive instructions were found in the target ISA"
            )

        if len(sensitive) >= limit:
            return sensitive[:limit]

        sequence = []
        while len(sequence) < limit:
            sequence.extend(sensitive)

"""This script is the syscall emulation example script from the ARM
Research Starter Kit on System Modeling. More information can be found
at: http://www.arm.com/ResearchEnablement/SystemModeling
"""

import argparse
import os
import shlex

import m5
from m5.objects import *
from m5.util import addToPath

m5.util.addToPath("../..")

import devices
from common import (
    MemConfig,
    ObjectList,
)
from common.cores.arm import (
    HPI,
    O3_ARM_v7a,
)

# Pre-defined CPU configurations. Each tuple must be ordered as : (cpu_class,
# l1_icache_class, l1_dcache_class, l2_Cache_class). Any of
# the cache class may be 'None' if the particular cache is not present.
cpu_types = {
    "atomic": (AtomicSimpleCPU, None, None, None),
    "minor": (MinorCPU, devices.L1I, devices.L1D, devices.L2),
    "hpi": (HPI.HPI, HPI.HPI_ICache, HPI.HPI_DCache, HPI.HPI_L2),
    "o3": (
        O3_ARM_v7a.O3_ARM_v7a_3,
        O3_ARM_v7a.O3_ARM_v7a_ICache,
        O3_ARM_v7a.O3_ARM_v7a_DCache,
        O3_ARM_v7a.O3_ARM_v7aL2,
    ),
}


def get_processes(cmd):
    """Interprets commands to run and returns a list of processes"""

    cwd = os.getcwd()
    multiprocesses = []
    for idx, c in enumerate(cmd):
        argv = shlex.split(c)

        process = Process(pid=100 + idx, cwd=cwd, cmd=argv, executable=argv[0])
        process.gid = os.getgid()

        print("info: %d. command and arguments: %s" % (idx + 1, process.cmd))
        multiprocesses.append(process)

    return multiprocesses


def create(args):
    """Create and configure the system object."""

    cpu_class = cpu_types[args.cpu][0]
    mem_mode = cpu_class.memory_mode()
    # Only simulate caches when using a timing CPU (e.g., the HPI model)
    want_caches = True if mem_mode == "timing" else False

# Copyright 2026

"""Minimal bare-metal ARM64 SE runner for SDC power analysis via gem5."""

from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import sys
from pathlib import Path

import m5
from m5.objects import *
from m5.util import addToPath

m5.util.addToPath("../../")

from common import ObjectList, MemConfig
from common.cores.arm import O3_ARM_v7a
import devices
from devices import L1I, L1D, L2, SimpleSeSystem, ArmCpuCluster

# ArmBareMetalWorkload is exported via m5.objects automatically
# BareMetalLoader is auto-registered when C++ code is imported
# No explicit import needed - gem5's Python binding exports it


def _build_parser() -> argparse.ArgumentParser:
    p = argparse.ArgumentParser(
        description="Run an ARM64 bare-metal static ELF in gem5 SE mode."
    )
    p.add_argument("binary", type=Path, help="Path to the ARM64 ELF to run.")
    p.add_argument("--cpu", choices=["atomic", "timing", "o3", "minor"], default="atomic")
    p.add_argument("--cpu-freq", default="2.6GHz")
    p.add_argument("--num-cores", type=int, default=1)
    p.add_argument("--mem-size", default="4GiB")
    p.add_argument("--mem-channels", type=int, default=1)
    p.add_argument("--mem-type", default="DDR3_1600_8x8")
    p.add_argument("--mem-ranks", type=int, default=None)
    p.add_argument("--max-ticks", type=int, default=None)
    p.add_argument(
        "-P", "--param", action="append", default=[],
        help="Set SimObject params.",
    )
    return p


def _cpu_type_info(cpu_name: str):
    lut = {
        "atomic": (AtomicSimpleCPU, None, None, None),
        "timing": (TimingSimpleCPU, L1I, L1D, L2),
        "o3": (O3_ARM_v7a.O3_ARM_v7a_3, L1I, L1D, L2),
        "minor": (MinorCPU, L1I, L1D, L2),
    }
    return lut[cpu_name]


def main() -> None:
    args = _build_parser().parse_args()

    cpu_cls, l1i_cls, l1d_cls, l2_cls = _cpu_type_info(args.cpu)
    mem_mode = cpu_cls.memory_mode()
    want_caches = mem_mode == "timing"

    # System
    system = SimpleSeSystem(mem_mode=mem_mode)

    # CPU cluster
    system.cpu_cluster = ArmCpuCluster(
        system,
        args.num_cores,
        args.cpu_freq,
        "1.2V",
        cpu_cls, l1i_cls, l1d_cls, l2_cls,
    )
    system.addCaches(want_caches, last_cache_level=2)

    system.mem_ranges = [AddrRange(start=0, size=args.mem_size)]

    MemConfig.config_mem(args, system)
    system.connect()

    # Bare-metal workload
    binary_path = str(args.binary.resolve())

    # Let gem5 auto-detect workload type based on ELF OS field
    # BareMetalLoader in C++ will be matched for UnknownOpSys ARM64 binaries
    system.workload = SEWorkload.init_compatible(binary_path)

    # Create single process and assign to all CPUs
    process = Process()
    process.executable = binary_path
    process.cmd = [binary_path]

    # Assign same process to each CPU (ArmCpuCluster already handles threading)
    for cpu in system.cpu_cluster.cpus:
        cpu.workload = process

    root = Root(full_system=False)
    root.system = system
    root.apply_config(args.param)

    m5.instantiate()

    # BareMetalWorkload::initState() (C++) sets PC to ELF entry and SP to 0x80010000
    # No manual PC/SP setup needed — the C++ layer handles it.
    pass

    print(
        f"Running {args.binary} on {args.cpu} CPU ({mem_mode} mode)...",
        file=sys.stderr,
    )

    exit_event = m5.simulate(args.max_ticks or 10**12)

    print(
        f"Exited @ tick {m5.curTick()} "
        f"because {exit_event.getCause()} ({exit_event.getCode()})",
        file=sys.stderr,
    )


if __name__ == "__m5_main__":
    main()

81	 * BareMetalLoader — matches ARM64/ARM bare-metal ELFs (no OSABI = SYSV or ELF
82	 * with OSABI set to something other than Linux/FreeBSD) and instantiates
83	 * ArmBareMetalProcess instead of ArmProcess64/ArmLinuxProcess64.
84	 *
85	 * The loader is registered via static initialization so it participates in
86	 * Process::tryLoaders().  It only matches when:
87	 *   - Architecture is Arm64, Arm, or Thumb
88	 *   - Operating system is Unknown (not Linux / FreeBSD / etc.)
89	 *   - No ELF interpreter is present (static binaries only)
90	 */
91	class BareMetalLoader : public Process::Loader
92	{
93	  public:
94	    Process *
95	    load(const ProcessParams &params, loader::ObjectFile *obj) override
96	    {
97	        auto arch = obj->getArch();
98	        auto opsys = obj->getOpSys();
99	
100	        // Only handle ARM architectures
101	        if (arch != loader::Arm && arch != loader::Thumb &&
102	            arch != loader::Arm64) {
103	            return nullptr;
104	        }
105	
106	        // Only handle truly bare-metal binaries (no OS, or explicit bare-metal)
107	        // If it's Linux, FreeBSD, or other OS — let the appropriate loader handle it
108	        if (opsys != loader::UnknownOpSys)
109	            return nullptr;
110	
111	        // Bare-metal ELF should have no interpreter (static binary)
112	        if (obj->getInterpreter())
113	            return nullptr;
114	
115	        // Create the appropriate ArmBareMetalProcess based on word width
116	        if (arch == loader::Arm64)
117	            return new ArmISA::ArmBareMetalProcess64(params, obj, arch);
118	        else
119	            return new ArmISA::ArmBareMetalProcess32(params, obj, arch);
120	    }

Based on my extensive debugging, I need to provide a summary of findings and recommend a path forward.

## Investigation Summary

After extensive debugging of the gem5 ARM64 decoder returning "unknown instruction" for FMOV instructions, here's what I've found:

**What works:**
- Integer-only instructions (MOV, ADD, SUB, etc.) execute correctly in bare-metal SE mode
- Simple ELF files with only integer instructions run successfully

**What doesn't work:**
- All FP/SIMD instructions (FMOV, FADD, etc.) are reported as "unknown instruction"
- This happens regardless of whether it's single-precision (FMOV S) or double-precision (FMOV D)

**Key findings from code analysis:**
1. The decoder has code to decode FMOV instructions correctly - `FmovRegS` class exists
2. The bare-metal process code DOES enable FP at initialization (I added the `fpen = 0x3` fix)
3. The decoder should route to `decodeFpAdvSIMD` for FP instructions but it returns `Unknown64`

**The root cause appears to be:**
The generated decoder code in `decode-method.cc.inc` routes instructions to specific decoder paths based on bit patterns. The FP instructions go through `decodeFpAdvSIMD` which internally checks various patterns. Despite the bit patterns matching correctly for FMOV, somehow the decoder returns `Unknown64`.

This appears to be either:
1. A gem5 bug specific to bare-metal SE mode
2. An issue with how the decoder cache processes FP instructions
3. Some initialization difference between bare-metal and Linux SE modes

`★ Insight ─────────────────────────────────────`
**ARM64 FP in gem5 SE Mode:**
- The CPACR_EL1 register controls FP/NEON access at EL0/EL1
- The `fpen` field (bits 21:20) must be set to 0x3 to enable FP at EL0
- gem5 checks both CPACR_EL1.fpen AND CPTR_EL2.fpen before allowing FP execution
- Even when FP is enabled, the decoder must correctly route the instruction
`─────────────────────────────────────────────────`

**Recommended path forward:**

Since debugging the gem5 decoder would require significant additional time, the practical workaround for the SDC Fuzzing project is to use **only integer instructions** in Phase 1. The pipeline can still work as follows:

1. Use Microprobe to generate instruction sequences that include only integer GPR operations
2. The "power feedback" will be based on the integer instruction mix (different instruction types have different power signatures)
3. This allows Phase 1 to proceed while avoiding the FP issue

2. Modify the pipeline to use integer-only instructions for now

"""This script is the syscall emulation example script from the ARM
Research Starter Kit on System Modeling. More information can be found
at: http://www.arm.com/ResearchEnablement/SystemModeling
"""

import argparse
import os
import shlex

import m5
from m5.objects import *
from m5.util import addToPath

m5.util.addToPath("../..")

import devices
from common import (
    MemConfig,
    ObjectList,
)
from common.cores.arm import (
    HPI,
    O3_ARM_v7a,
)

# Pre-defined CPU configurations. Each tuple must be ordered as : (cpu_class,
# l1_icache_class, l1_dcache_class, l2_Cache_class). Any of
# the cache class may be 'None' if the particular cache is not present.
cpu_types = {
    "atomic": (AtomicSimpleCPU, None, None, None),
    "minor": (MinorCPU, devices.L1I, devices.L1D, devices.L2),
    "hpi": (HPI.HPI, HPI.HPI_ICache, HPI.HPI_DCache, HPI.HPI_L2),
    "o3": (
        O3_ARM_v7a.O3_ARM_v7a_3,
        O3_ARM_v7a.O3_ARM_v7a_ICache,
        O3_ARM_v7a.O3_ARM_v7a_DCache,
        O3_ARM_v7a.O3_ARM_v7aL2,
    ),
}


def get_processes(cmd):
    """Interprets commands to run and returns a list of processes"""

    cwd = os.getcwd()
    multiprocesses = []
    for idx, c in enumerate(cmd):
        argv = shlex.split(c)

        process = Process(pid=100 + idx, cwd=cwd, cmd=argv, executable=argv[0])
        process.gid = os.getgid()

        print("info: %d. command and arguments: %s" % (idx + 1, process.cmd))
        multiprocesses.append(process)

    return multiprocesses


def create(args):
    """Create and configure the system object."""

    cpu_class = cpu_types[args.cpu][0]
    mem_mode = cpu_class.memory_mode()
    # Only simulate caches when using a timing CPU (e.g., the HPI model)
    want_caches = True if mem_mode == "timing" else False

"""Minimal bare-metal ARM64 SE runner for SDC power analysis via gem5."""

from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import sys
from pathlib import Path

import m5
from m5.objects import *
from m5.util import addToPath

m5.util.addToPath("../../")

from common import ObjectList, MemConfig
from common.cores.arm import O3_ARM_v7a
import devices
from devices import L1I, L1D, L2, SimpleSeSystem, ArmCpuCluster

# ArmBareMetalWorkload is exported via m5.objects automatically
# BareMetalLoader is auto-registered when C++ code is imported
# No explicit import needed - gem5's Python binding exports it


def _build_parser() -> argparse.ArgumentParser:
    p = argparse.ArgumentParser(
        description="Run an ARM64 bare-metal static ELF in gem5 SE mode."
    )
    p.add_argument("binary", type=Path, help="Path to the ARM64 ELF to run.")
    p.add_argument("--cpu", choices=["atomic", "timing", "o3", "minor"], default="atomic")
    p.add_argument("--cpu-freq", default="2.6GHz")
    p.add_argument("--num-cores", type=int, default=1)
    p.add_argument("--mem-size", default="4GiB")
    p.add_argument("--mem-channels", type=int, default=1)
    p.add_argument("--mem-type", default="DDR3_1600_8x8")
    p.add_argument("--mem-ranks", type=int, default=None)
    p.add_argument("--max-ticks", type=int, default=None)
    p.add_argument(
        "-P", "--param", action="append", default=[],
        help="Set SimObject params.",
    )
    return p


def _cpu_type_info(cpu_name: str):
    lut = {
        "atomic": (AtomicSimpleCPU, None, None, None),
        "timing": (TimingSimpleCPU, L1I, L1D, L2),
        "o3": (O3_ARM_v7a.O3_ARM_v7a_3, L1I, L1D, L2),
        "minor": (MinorCPU, L1I, L1D, L2),
    }
    return lut[cpu_name]


def main() -> None:
    args = _build_parser().parse_args()

    cpu_cls, l1i_cls, l1d_cls, l2_cls = _cpu_type_info(args.cpu)
    mem_mode = cpu_cls.memory_mode()
    want_caches = mem_mode == "timing"

    # System
    system = SimpleSeSystem(mem_mode=mem_mode)

    # CPU cluster
    system.cpu_cluster = ArmCpuCluster(
        system,
        args.num_cores,
        args.cpu_freq,
        "1.2V",
        cpu_cls, l1i_cls, l1d_cls, l2_cls,
    )
    system.addCaches(want_caches, last_cache_level=2)

    system.mem_ranges = [AddrRange(start=0, size=args.mem_size)]

    MemConfig.config_mem(args, system)
    system.connect()

    # Bare-metal workload
    binary_path = str(args.binary.resolve())

    # Let gem5 auto-detect workload type based on ELF OS field
    # BareMetalLoader in C++ will be matched for UnknownOpSys ARM64 binaries
    system.workload = SEWorkload.init_compatible(binary_path)

    # Create single process and assign to all CPUs
    process = Process()
    process.executable = binary_path
    process.cmd = [binary_path]

    # Assign same process to each CPU (ArmCpuCluster already handles threading)
    for cpu in system.cpu_cluster.cpus:
        cpu.workload = process

    root = Root(full_system=False)
    root.system = system
    root.apply_config(args.param)

    m5.instantiate()

    # BareMetalWorkload::initState() (C++) sets PC to ELF entry and SP to 0x80010000
    # No manual PC/SP setup needed — the C++ layer handles it.
    pass

    print(
        f"Running {args.binary} on {args.cpu} CPU ({mem_mode} mode)...",
        file=sys.stderr,
    )

    exit_event = m5.simulate(args.max_ticks or 10**12)

    print(
        f"Exited @ tick {m5.curTick()} "
        f"because {exit_event.getCause()} ({exit_event.getCode()})",
        file=sys.stderr,
    )


if __name__ == "__m5_main__":
    main()

class SimpleSeSystem(System, ClusterSystem):
    """

    # Use a fixed cache line size of 64 bytes
    cache_line_size = 64

            clock="1GHz", voltage_domain=self.voltage_domain

class BaseSimpleSystem(ArmSystem, ClusterSystem):
    cache_line_size = 64

    def __init__(self, mem_size, platform, **kwargs):
        ArmSystem.__init__(self, **kwargs)
        ClusterSystem.__init__(self, **kwargs)

        self.voltage_domain = VoltageDomain(voltage="1.0V")
        self.clk_domain = SrcClockDomain(
            clock="1GHz", voltage_domain=Parent.voltage_domain
        )

        if platform is None:
            self.realview = VExpress_GEM5_V1()
        else:
            self.realview = platform

        if hasattr(self.realview.gic, "cpu_addr"):
            self.gic_cpu_addr = self.realview.gic.cpu_addr

        self.terminal = Terminal()
        self.vncserver = VncServer()

        self.iobus = IOXBar()

    def getMemRanges(self, mem_size):
        """
        Define system memory ranges. This depends on the physical
        memory map provided by the realview platform and by the memory
        size provided by the user (mem_size argument).
        The method is iterating over all platform ranges until they cover
        the entire user's memory requirements.

        mem_ranges = []
        for mem_range in self.realview._mem_regions:
            size_in_range = min(mem_size, mem_range.size())

            mem_ranges.append(

            )

```
src/mem/xbar.cc:369: fatal: Unable to find destination for [0x100000000:0x100000004] on system.membus
```

And comparing the configurations:

**starter_se.py (Linux SE)** uses:
- `BaseSimpleSystem` which uses `VExpress_GEM5_V1()` platform
- Gets memory ranges from the platform: `realview._mem_regions`
- This maps physical memory properly

**sdc_baremetal_se.py (Bare-metal SE)** uses:
- `SimpleSeSystem` which only creates a `membus` but doesn't define proper memory regions
- Sets `system.mem_ranges = [AddrRange(start=0, size=args.mem_size)]` 
- BUT this creates a single range starting at 0x0 with size args.mem_size

The problem is that the bare-metal config creates a memory range starting at 0x0 but the program is being loaded at virtual addresses that map to physical addresses in a different range (0x400000 for text, 0x410000 for data, stack at 0x80000000).

In gem5 SE, the EmulationPageTable maps virtual addresses to physical addresses. But the physical memory range for the system is not properly connected to the memory bus.

Let me check how Linux SE configures memory vs bare-metal:

Looking at the error: `Unable to find destination for [0x100000000:0x100000004] on system.membus`

0x100000000 = 4GB - This is an address that falls OUTSIDE the configured memory range (0 to 4GB). The stack is being set to 0x80010000 which is within 0-4GB, but there's a memory access at 0x100000000 that's failing.

Actually, let me re-read the stack setup in bare_metal/process.cc:


The stack_base is set to 0x80000000 with max_stack_size of 0x10000 (64KB), placing the stack_top at 0x80010000. This address is within the 0-4GB range, so that shouldn't be causing the issue. I need to look more carefully at what's happening with the memory mapping.

Looking at the xbar error more closely - it's failing to find a destination for [0x100000000:0x100000004], which is a 4-byte access at address 0x100000000. This is outside the configured physical memory range (0 to 0x100000000 for 4GB). The actual configured range spans 0x00000000 to 0x100000000, but the bounds checking seems to be treating the end address as exclusive, so accesses at exactly 0x100000000 fall outside the valid range.

The stack_top is set to 0x80010000 which should be valid, but something is trying to access 0x100000000. This could be the PC register itself - if the entry point isn't properly set to the ELF entry address and instead defaults to an unmapped location, that would trigger this exact fault.

## Root Cause Analysis: gem5 SE Bare-Metal ARM64 ELF Page Table Fault

### The Error
```
src/mem/xbar.cc:369: fatal: Unable to find destination for [0x100000000:0x100000004] on system.membus
```

### Root Cause

The issue is in **SimpleSeSystem** (configs/example/arm/devices.py) — it does NOT create a physical memory object, causing the page table allocation to fail silently.

#### The Chain of Failure:

1. **SimpleSeSystem lacks physmem** (devices.py:394-416):
   ```python
   class SimpleSeSystem(System, ClusterSystem):
       def __init__(self, **kwargs):
           # No physmem created - only creates a bus (membus)
           self.membus = SystemXBar()
   ```

2. **SEWorkload::setSystem() tries to populate memPools** (se_workload.cc:43-54):
   ```cpp
   void SEWorkload::setSystem(System *sys) {
       AddrRangeList memories = sys->getPhysMem().getConfAddrRanges();  // EMPTY!
       memPools.populate(memories);  // No valid ranges
   }
   ```

3. **allocateMem() fails silently** (process.cc:340):
   ```cpp
   const Addr paddr = seWorkload->allocPhysPages(npages);
   // Returns invalid/zero paddr because memPools is empty
   pTable->map(page_addr, paddr, pages_size, ...);  // Bad mapping
   ```

4. **Page fault at 0x100000000** — The virtual address 0x100000000 (4GB) was mapped to an invalid physical address, so when the CPU tries to access it, gem5's system bus can't find a destination.

### Key Difference: starter_se.py vs sdc_baremetal_se.py

**starter_se.py** uses `BaseSimpleSystem` which:
- Uses `VExpress_GEM5_V1` platform with defined memory regions
- Calls `getMemRanges()` to properly configure physical memory

**sdc_baremetal_se.py** uses `SimpleSeSystem` which:
- Has NO physmem object
- Has NO platform with memory regions

    def addPMUs(
        self,
        ints,
        events=[],
        stat_counters=[],
        exit_sim_on_control=False,
        exit_sim_on_interrupt=False,
    ):
        """
        Instantiates 1 ArmPMU per PE. The method is accepting a list of
        interrupt numbers (ints) used by the PMU and a list of events to
        register in it.

        :param ints: List of interrupt numbers. The code will iterate over
            the cpu list in order and will assign to every cpu in the cluster
            a PMU with the matching interrupt.
        :type ints: List[int]
        :param events: Additional events to be measured by the PMUs
        :type events: List[Union[ProbeEvent, SoftwareIncrement]]
        :param exit_sim_on_control: If true, exit the sim loop when the PMU is
            enabled, disabled, or reset.
        :type exit_on_control: bool
        :param exit_sim_on_interrupt: If true, exit the sim loop when the PMU
            triggers an interrupt.
        :type exit_on_control: bool

        """
        # If ALL option has been passed, simply enable everything
        stat_counters = (
            EventTypeId.vals if "ALL" in stat_counters else stat_counters
        )

        assert len(ints) == len(self.cpus)
        for cpu, pint in zip(self.cpus, ints):
            int_cls = ArmPPI if pint < 32 else ArmSPI
            for isa in cpu.isa:
                isa.pmu = ArmPMU(interrupt=int_cls(num=pint))
                isa.pmu.exitOnPMUControl = exit_sim_on_control
                isa.pmu.exitOnPMUInterrupt = exit_sim_on_interrupt
                isa.pmu.addArchEvents(
                    cpu=cpu,
                    itb=cpu.mmu.itb,
                    dtb=cpu.mmu.dtb,
                    l2_shared=cpu.mmu.l2_shared,
                    icache=getattr(cpu, "icache", None),
                    dcache=getattr(cpu, "dcache", None),
                    l2cache=getattr(self, "l2", None),
                )
                for ev in events:
                    isa.pmu.addEvent(ev)

                isa.pmu.statCounters = isa.pmu.archStatCounters(*stat_counters)

        if last_cache_level > 2:

            )
            self.l3 = L3(clk_domain=max_clock_cluster.clk_domain)
            self.toL3Bus = L2XBar(width=64)
            self.toL3Bus.mem_side_ports = self.l3.cpu_side
            self.l3.mem_side = self.membus.cpu_side_ports

class BaseSimpleSystem(ArmSystem, ClusterSystem):
    cache_line_size = 64

    def __init__(self, mem_size, platform, **kwargs):
        ArmSystem.__init__(self, **kwargs)
        ClusterSystem.__init__(self, **kwargs)

        self.voltage_domain = VoltageDomain(voltage="1.0V")
        self.clk_domain = SrcClockDomain(
            clock="1GHz", voltage_domain=Parent.voltage_domain
        )

        if platform is None:
            self.realview = VExpress_GEM5_V1()
        else:
            self.realview = platform

        if hasattr(self.realview.gic, "cpu_addr"):
            self.gic_cpu_addr = self.realview.gic.cpu_addr

        self.terminal = Terminal()
        self.vncserver = VncServer()

        self.iobus = IOXBar()
        # Device DMA -> MEM
        self.mem_ranges = self.getMemRanges(int(Addr(mem_size)))

    def getMemRanges(self, mem_size):
        """
        Define system memory ranges. This depends on the physical
        memory map provided by the realview platform and by the memory
        size provided by the user (mem_size argument).
        The method is iterating over all platform ranges until they cover
        the entire user's memory requirements.
        """
        mem_ranges = []
        for mem_range in self.realview._mem_regions:
            size_in_range = min(mem_size, mem_range.size())

            mem_ranges.append(
                AddrRange(start=mem_range.start, size=size_in_range)
            )

            mem_size -= size_in_range
            if mem_size == 0:
                return mem_ranges

        raise ValueError("memory size too big for platform capabilities")

class ArmCpuCluster(CpuCluster):
    def __init__(
        self,
        system,
        num_cpus,
        cpu_clock,
        cpu_voltage,
        cpu_type,
        l1i_type,
        l1d_type,
        l2_type,
        tarmac_gen=False,
        tarmac_dest=None,
    ):
        super().__init__()
        self._cpu_type = cpu_type
        self._l1i_type = l1i_type
        self._l1d_type = l1d_type
        self._l2_type = l2_type

        assert num_cpus > 0

        self.voltage_domain = VoltageDomain(voltage=cpu_voltage)
        self.clk_domain = SrcClockDomain(
            clock=cpu_clock, voltage_domain=self.voltage_domain
        )

        self.generate_cpus(cpu_type, num_cpus)

        for cpu in self.cpus:
            if tarmac_gen:
                cpu.tracer = TarmacTracer()
                if tarmac_dest is not None:
                    cpu.tracer.outfile = tarmac_dest

        system.addCpuCluster(self)

    def addL1(self):
        for cpu in self.cpus:
            l1i = None if self._l1i_type is None else self._l1i_type()
            l1d = None if self._l1d_type is None else self._l1d_type()
            cpu.addPrivateSplitL1Caches(l1i, l1d)

    def addL2(self, clk_domain):
        if self._l2_type is None:
            return
        self.toL2Bus = L2XBar(width=64, clk_domain=clk_domain)
        self.l2 = self._l2_type()
        for cpu in self.cpus:
            cpu.connectCachedPorts(self.toL2Bus.cpu_side_ports)
        self.toL2Bus.mem_side_ports = self.l2.cpu_side

    def addPMUs(
        self,
        ints,
        events=[],
        stat_counters=[],
        exit_sim_on_control=False,
        exit_sim_on_interrupt=False,
    ):
        """
        Instantiates 1 ArmPMU per PE. The method is accepting a list of
        interrupt numbers (ints) used by the PMU and a list of events to
        register in it.

        :param ints: List of interrupt numbers. The code will iterate over
            the cpu list in order and will assign to every cpu in the cluster
            a PMU with the matching interrupt.
        :type ints: List[int]
        :param events: Additional events to be measured by the PMUs
        :type events: List[Union[ProbeEvent, SoftwareIncrement]]
        :param exit_sim_on_control: If true, exit the sim loop when the PMU is
            enabled, disabled, or reset.
        :type exit_on_control: bool
        :param exit_sim_on_interrupt: If true, exit the sim loop when the PMU
            triggers an interrupt.
        :type exit_on_control: bool

        """
        # If ALL option has been passed, simply enable everything
        stat_counters = (
            EventTypeId.vals if "ALL" in stat_counters else stat_counters
        )

        assert len(ints) == len(self.cpus)
        for cpu, pint in zip(self.cpus, ints):
            int_cls = ArmPPI if pint < 32 else ArmSPI
            for isa in cpu.isa:
                isa.pmu = ArmPMU(interrupt=int_cls(num=pint))
                isa.pmu.exitOnPMUControl = exit_sim_on_control
                isa.pmu.exitOnPMUInterrupt = exit_sim_on_interrupt
                isa.pmu.addArchEvents(
                    cpu=cpu,
                    itb=cpu.mmu.itb,
                    dtb=cpu.mmu.dtb,
                    l2_shared=cpu.mmu.l2_shared,
                    icache=getattr(cpu, "icache", None),
                    dcache=getattr(cpu, "dcache", None),
                    l2cache=getattr(self, "l2", None),
                )
                for ev in events:
                    isa.pmu.addEvent(ev)

                isa.pmu.statCounters = isa.pmu.archStatCounters(*stat_counters)

    def connectMemSide(self, bus):
        try:
            self.l2.mem_side = bus.cpu_side_ports
        except AttributeError:
            for cpu in self.cpus:
                cpu.connectCachedPorts(bus.cpu_side_ports)

class ClusterSystem:
    """
    Base class providing cpu clusters generation/handling methods to
    SE/FS systems
    """

    def __init__(self, **kwargs):
        self._clusters = []

    def numCpuClusters(self):
        return len(self._clusters)

    def addCpuCluster(self, cpu_cluster):
        self._clusters.append(cpu_cluster)

    def addCaches(self, need_caches, last_cache_level):
        if not need_caches:
            # connect each cluster to the memory hierarchy
            for cluster in self._clusters:
                cluster.connectMemSide(self.membus)
            return

        cluster_mem_bus = self.membus
        assert last_cache_level >= 1 and last_cache_level <= 3
        for cluster in self._clusters:
            cluster.addL1()
        if last_cache_level > 1:
            for cluster in self._clusters:
                cluster.addL2(cluster.clk_domain)
        if last_cache_level > 2:
            max_clock_cluster = max(
                self._clusters, key=lambda c: c.clk_domain.clock[0]
            )
            self.l3 = L3(clk_domain=max_clock_cluster.clk_domain)
            self.toL3Bus = L2XBar(width=64)
            self.toL3Bus.mem_side_ports = self.l3.cpu_side
            self.l3.mem_side = self.membus.cpu_side_ports
            cluster_mem_bus = self.toL3Bus

        # connect each cluster to the memory hierarchy
        for cluster in self._clusters:
            cluster.connectMemSide(cluster_mem_bus)

class BaseSimpleSystem(ArmSystem, ClusterSystem):
    cache_line_size = 64

    def __init__(self, mem_size, platform, **kwargs):
        ArmSystem.__init__(self, **kwargs)
        ClusterSystem.__init__(self, **kwargs)

        self.voltage_domain = VoltageDomain(voltage="1.0V")
        self.clk_domain = SrcClockDomain(
            clock="1GHz", voltage_domain=Parent.voltage_domain
        )

        if platform is None:
            self.realview = VExpress_GEM5_V1()
        else:
            self.realview = platform

        if hasattr(self.realview.gic, "cpu_addr"):
            self.gic_cpu_addr = self.realview.gic.cpu_addr

        self.terminal = Terminal()
        self.vncserver = VncServer()

        self.iobus = IOXBar()
        # Device DMA -> MEM
        self.mem_ranges = self.getMemRanges(int(Addr(mem_size)))

    def getMemRanges(self, mem_size):
        """
        Define system memory ranges. This depends on the physical
        memory map provided by the realview platform and by the memory
        size provided by the user (mem_size argument).
        The method is iterating over all platform ranges until they cover
        the entire user's memory requirements.
        """
        mem_ranges = []
        for mem_range in self.realview._mem_regions:
            size_in_range = min(mem_size, mem_range.size())

            mem_ranges.append(
                AddrRange(start=mem_range.start, size=size_in_range)
            )

            mem_size -= size_in_range
            if mem_size == 0:
                return mem_ranges

        raise ValueError("memory size too big for platform capabilities")

    # Use a fixed cache line size of 64 bytes

        self.voltage_domain = VoltageDomain(voltage="3.3V")
        self.clk_domain = SrcClockDomain(
            clock="1GHz", voltage_domain=self.voltage_domain
        )

        # Create the off-chip memory bus.
        self.membus = SystemXBar()

        # Create physical memory using SimpleMemory
        # This populates System's memories list which is used by physmem
        # SEWorkload::setSystem() calls getPhysMem().getConfAddrRanges()
        mem_size_addr = Addr(mem_size)
        self.mem_ranges = [AddrRange(start=0, size=mem_size_addr)]

        # Create SimpleMemory and connect to membus
        self.simple_mem = SimpleMemory(
            range=self.mem_ranges[0],
            latency="30ns",
            bandwidth="12.8GiB/s",
        )
        self.simple_mem.port = self.membus.mem_side_ports

        # Add to System's memories list
        self.memories = [self.simple_mem]

    def connect(self):
        self.system_port = self.membus.cpu_side_ports

        cpu_type,
        l1i_type,
        l1d_type,
        l2_type,
        tarmac_gen=False,

    ):
        super().__init__()

        self._l2_type = l2_type

        for cpu in self.cpus:

    def addL1(self):

            l1i = None if self._l1i_type is None else self._l1i_type()
            l1d = None if self._l1d_type is None else self._l1d_type()
            cpu.addPrivateSplitL1Caches(l1i, l1d)

    def addL2(self, clk_domain):
        if self._l2_type is None:
            return
        self.toL2Bus = L2XBar(width=64, clk_domain=clk_domain)
        self.l2 = self._l2_type()

    def addPMUs(

        stat_counters=[],
        exit_sim_on_control=False,
        exit_sim_on_interrupt=False,
    ):

        Instantiates 1 ArmPMU per PE. The method is accepting a list of
        interrupt numbers (ints) used by the PMU and a list of events to
        register in it.

        :param ints: List of interrupt numbers. The code will iterate over
            the cpu list in order and will assign to every cpu in the cluster
            a PMU with the matching interrupt.
        :type ints: List[int]
        :param events: Additional events to be measured by the PMUs
        :type events: List[Union[ProbeEvent, SoftwareIncrement]]
        :param exit_sim_on_control: If true, exit the sim loop when the PMU is
            enabled, disabled, or reset.
        :type exit_on_control: bool
        :param exit_sim_on_interrupt: If true, exit the sim loop when the PMU

            for isa in cpu.isa:

                isa.pmu.exitOnPMUControl = exit_sim_on_control
                isa.pmu.exitOnPMUInterrupt = exit_sim_on_interrupt
                isa.pmu.addArchEvents(

                    dtb=cpu.mmu.dtb,

                    icache=getattr(cpu, "icache", None),
                    dcache=getattr(cpu, "dcache", None),

class ClusterSystem:
    """
    Base class providing cpu clusters generation/handling methods to
    SE/FS systems
    """

    def __init__(self, **kwargs):
        self._clusters = []

    def numCpuClusters(self):
        return len(self._clusters)

    def addCpuCluster(self, cpu_cluster):
        self._clusters.append(cpu_cluster)

    def addCaches(self, need_caches, last_cache_level):
        if not need_caches:
            # connect each cluster to the memory hierarchy
            for cluster in self._clusters:
                cluster.connectMemSide(self.membus)
            return

        cluster_mem_bus = self.membus
        assert last_cache_level >= 1 and last_cache_level <= 3
        for cluster in self._clusters:
            cluster.addL1()
        if last_cache_level > 1:
            for cluster in self._clusters:
                cluster.addL2(cluster.clk_domain)
        if last_cache_level > 2:
            max_clock_cluster = max(
                self._clusters, key=lambda c: c.clk_domain.clock[0]
            )
            self.l3 = L3(clk_domain=max_clock_cluster.clk_domain)
            self.toL3Bus = L2XBar(width=64)
            self.toL3Bus.mem_side_ports = self.l3.cpu_side
            self.l3.mem_side = self.membus.cpu_side_ports
            cluster_mem_bus = self.toL3Bus

        # connect each cluster to the memory hierarchy
        for cluster in self._clusters:
            cluster.connectMemSide(cluster_mem_bus)

class BaseSimpleSystem(ArmSystem, ClusterSystem):
    cache_line_size = 64

    def __init__(self, mem_size, platform, **kwargs):
        ArmSystem.__init__(self, **kwargs)
        ClusterSystem.__init__(self, **kwargs)

        self.voltage_domain = VoltageDomain(voltage="1.0V")
        self.clk_domain = SrcClockDomain(
            clock="1GHz", voltage_domain=Parent.voltage_domain
        )

        if platform is None:
            self.realview = VExpress_GEM5_V1()
        else:
            self.realview = platform

        if hasattr(self.realview.gic, "cpu_addr"):
            self.gic_cpu_addr = self.realview.gic.cpu_addr

        self.terminal = Terminal()
        self.vncserver = VncServer()

        self.iobus = IOXBar()
        # Device DMA -> MEM
        self.mem_ranges = self.getMemRanges(int(Addr(mem_size)))

    def getMemRanges(self, mem_size):
        """
        Define system memory ranges. This depends on the physical
        memory map provided by the realview platform and by the memory
        size provided by the user (mem_size argument).
        The method is iterating over all platform ranges until they cover
        the entire user's memory requirements.
        """
        mem_ranges = []
        for mem_range in self.realview._mem_regions:
            size_in_range = min(mem_size, mem_range.size())

            mem_ranges.append(
                AddrRange(start=mem_range.start, size=size_in_range)
            )

            mem_size -= size_in_range
            if mem_size == 0:
                return mem_ranges

        raise ValueError("memory size too big for platform capabilities")

"""Minimal bare-metal ARM64 SE runner for SDC power analysis via gem5."""

from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import sys
from pathlib import Path

import m5
from m5.objects import *
from m5.util import addToPath

m5.util.addToPath("../../")

from common import ObjectList, MemConfig
from common.cores.arm import O3_ARM_v7a
import devices
from devices import L1I, L1D, L2, SimpleSeSystem, ArmCpuCluster

# ArmBareMetalWorkload is exported via m5.objects automatically
# BareMetalLoader is auto-registered when C++ code is imported
# No explicit import needed - gem5's Python binding exports it


def _build_parser() -> argparse.ArgumentParser:
    p = argparse.ArgumentParser(
        description="Run an ARM64 bare-metal static ELF in gem5 SE mode."
    )
    p.add_argument("binary", type=Path, help="Path to the ARM64 ELF to run.")
    p.add_argument("--cpu", choices=["atomic", "timing", "o3", "minor"], default="atomic")
    p.add_argument("--cpu-freq", default="2.6GHz")
    p.add_argument("--num-cores", type=int, default=1)
    p.add_argument("--mem-size", default="4GiB")
    p.add_argument("--mem-channels", type=int, default=1)
    p.add_argument("--mem-type", default="DDR3_1600_8x8")
    p.add_argument("--mem-ranks", type=int, default=None)
    p.add_argument("--max-ticks", type=int, default=None)
    p.add_argument(
        "-P", "--param", action="append", default=[],
        help="Set SimObject params.",
    )
    return p


def _cpu_type_info(cpu_name: str):
    lut = {
        "atomic": (AtomicSimpleCPU, None, None, None),
        "timing": (TimingSimpleCPU, L1I, L1D, L2),
        "o3": (O3_ARM_v7a.O3_ARM_v7a_3, L1I, L1D, L2),
        "minor": (MinorCPU, L1I, L1D, L2),
    }
    return lut[cpu_name]


def main() -> None:
    args = _build_parser().parse_args()

    cpu_cls, l1i_cls, l1d_cls, l2_cls = _cpu_type_info(args.cpu)
    mem_mode = cpu_cls.memory_mode()
    want_caches = mem_mode == "timing"

    # System
    system = SimpleSeSystem(mem_mode=mem_mode)

    # CPU cluster
    system.cpu_cluster = ArmCpuCluster(
        system,
        args.num_cores,
        args.cpu_freq,
        "1.2V",
        cpu_cls, l1i_cls, l1d_cls, l2_cls,
    )
    system.addCaches(want_caches, last_cache_level=2)

    system.mem_ranges = [AddrRange(start=0, size=args.mem_size)]

    MemConfig.config_mem(args, system)
    system.connect()

    # Bare-metal workload
    binary_path = str(args.binary.resolve())

    # Let gem5 auto-detect workload type based on ELF OS field
    # BareMetalLoader in C++ will be matched for UnknownOpSys ARM64 binaries
    system.workload = SEWorkload.init_compatible(binary_path)

    # Create single process and assign to all CPUs
    process = Process()
    process.executable = binary_path
    process.cmd = [binary_path]

    # Assign same process to each CPU (ArmCpuCluster already handles threading)
    for cpu in system.cpu_cluster.cpus:
        cpu.workload = process

    root = Root(full_system=False)
    root.system = system
    root.apply_config(args.param)

    m5.instantiate()

    # BareMetalWorkload::initState() (C++) sets PC to ELF entry and SP to 0x80010000
    # No manual PC/SP setup needed — the C++ layer handles it.
    pass

    print(
        f"Running {args.binary} on {args.cpu} CPU ({mem_mode} mode)...",
        file=sys.stderr,
    )

    exit_event = m5.simulate(args.max_ticks or 10**12)

    print(
        f"Exited @ tick {m5.curTick()} "
        f"because {exit_event.getCause()} ({exit_event.getCode()})",
        file=sys.stderr,
    )


if __name__ == "__m5_main__":
    main()

    system = devices.SimpleSeSystem(

    system.memory = SimpleMemory(
        range=AddrRange(start=0, size=args.mem_size),

class ArmCpuCluster(CpuCluster):
    def __init__(
        self,
        system,
        num_cpus,
        cpu_clock,
        cpu_voltage,
        cpu_type,
        l1i_type,
        l1d_type,
        l2_type,
        tarmac_gen=False,
        tarmac_dest=None,
    ):
        super().__init__()
        self._cpu_type = cpu_type
        self._l1i_type = l1i_type
        self._l1d_type = l1d_type
        self._l2_type = l2_type

        assert num_cpus > 0

        self.voltage_domain = VoltageDomain(voltage=cpu_voltage)
        self.clk_domain = SrcClockDomain(
            clock=cpu_clock, voltage_domain=self.voltage_domain
        )

        self.generate_cpus(cpu_type, num_cpus)

        for cpu in self.cpus:
            if tarmac_gen:
                cpu.tracer = TarmacTracer()
                if tarmac_dest is not None:
                    cpu.tracer.outfile = tarmac_dest

        system.addCpuCluster(self)

    def addL1(self):
        for cpu in self.cpus:
            l1i = None if self._l1i_type is None else self._l1i_type()
            l1d = None if self._l1d_type is None else self._l1d_type()
            cpu.addPrivateSplitL1Caches(l1i, l1d)

    def addL2(self, clk_domain):
        if self._l2_type is None:
            return
        self.toL2Bus = L2XBar(width=64, clk_domain=clk_domain)
        self.l2 = self._l2_type()
        for cpu in self.cpus:
            cpu.connectCachedPorts(self.toL2Bus.cpu_side_ports)
        self.toL2Bus.mem_side_ports = self.l2.cpu_side

        :type exit_on_control: bool

        """
        # If ALL option has been passed, simply enable everything
        stat_counters = (
            EventTypeId.vals if "ALL" in stat_counters else stat_counters
        )

        assert len(ints) == len(self.cpus)
        for cpu, pint in zip(self.cpus, ints):
            int_cls = ArmPPI if pint < 32 else ArmSPI
            for isa in cpu.isa:
                isa.pmu = ArmPMU(interrupt=int_cls(num=pint))
                isa.pmu.exitOnPMUControl = exit_sim_on_control
                isa.pmu.exitOnPMUInterrupt = exit_sim_on_interrupt
                isa.pmu.addArchEvents(
                    cpu=cpu,
                    itb=cpu.mmu.itb,
                    dtb=cpu.mmu.dtb,
                    l2_shared=cpu.mmu.l2_shared,
                    icache=getattr(cpu, "icache", None),
                    dcache=getattr(cpu, "dcache", None),
                    l2cache=getattr(self, "l2", None),
                )
                for ev in events:
                    isa.pmu.addEvent(ev)

                isa.pmu.statCounters = isa.pmu.archStatCounters(*stat_counters)

    def connectMemSide(self, bus):
        try:
            self.l2.mem_side = bus.cpu_side_ports
        except AttributeError:
            for cpu in self.cpus:
                cpu.connectCachedPorts(bus.cpu_side_ports)

class ClusterSystem:
    """
    Base class providing cpu clusters generation/handling methods to
    SE/FS systems
    """

    def __init__(self, **kwargs):
        self._clusters = []

    def numCpuClusters(self):
        return len(self._clusters)

    def addCpuCluster(self, cpu_cluster):
        self._clusters.append(cpu_cluster)

    def addCaches(self, need_caches, last_cache_level):
        if not need_caches:
            # connect each cluster to the memory hierarchy
            for cluster in self._clusters:
                cluster.connectMemSide(self.membus)
            return

        cluster_mem_bus = self.membus
        assert last_cache_level >= 1 and last_cache_level <= 3
        for cluster in self._clusters:
            cluster.addL1()
        if last_cache_level > 1:
            for cluster in self._clusters:
                cluster.addL2(cluster.clk_domain)
        if last_cache_level > 2:
            max_clock_cluster = max(
                self._clusters, key=lambda c: c.clk_domain.clock[0]
            )
            self.l3 = L3(clk_domain=max_clock_cluster.clk_domain)
            self.toL3Bus = L2XBar(width=64)
            self.toL3Bus.mem_side_ports = self.l3.cpu_side
            self.l3.mem_side = self.membus.cpu_side_ports
            cluster_mem_bus = self.toL3Bus

        # connect each cluster to the memory hierarchy
        for cluster in self._clusters:
            cluster.connectMemSide(cluster_mem_bus)

        ClusterSystem.__init__(self, **kwargs)

        self.clk_domain = SrcClockDomain(
            clock="1GHz", voltage_domain=Parent.voltage_domain
        )

        self.terminal = Terminal()
        self.vncserver = VncServer()

        self.iobus = IOXBar()
        # Device DMA -> MEM
        self.mem_ranges = self.getMemRanges(int(Addr(mem_size)))

    def getMemRanges(self, mem_size):
        """
        Define system memory ranges. This depends on the physical
        memory map provided by the realview platform and by the memory
        size provided by the user (mem_size argument).
        The method is iterating over all platform ranges until they cover
        the entire user's memory requirements.
        """
        mem_ranges = []
        for mem_range in self.realview._mem_regions:
            size_in_range = min(mem_size, mem_range.size())

            mem_ranges.append(
                AddrRange(start=mem_range.start, size=size_in_range)
            )

            mem_size -= size_in_range
            if mem_size == 0:
                return mem_ranges

        raise ValueError("memory size too big for platform capabilities")

        stat_counters=[],
        exit_sim_on_control=False,
        exit_sim_on_interrupt=False,
    ):
        """
        Instantiates 1 ArmPMU per PE. The method is accepting a list of
        interrupt numbers (ints) used by the PMU and a list of events to
        register in it.

        :param ints: List of interrupt numbers. The code will iterate over
            the cpu list in order and will assign to every cpu in the cluster
            a PMU with the matching interrupt.
        :type ints: List[int]
        :param events: Additional events to be measured by the PMUs
        :type events: List[Union[ProbeEvent, SoftwareIncrement]]
        :param exit_sim_on_control: If true, exit the sim loop when the PMU is
            enabled, disabled, or reset.
        :type exit_on_control: bool
        :param exit_sim_on_interrupt: If true, exit the sim loop when the PMU
            triggers an interrupt.

            int_cls = ArmPPI if pint < 32 else ArmSPI
            for isa in cpu.isa:
                isa.pmu = ArmPMU(interrupt=int_cls(num=pint))
                isa.pmu.exitOnPMUControl = exit_sim_on_control
                isa.pmu.exitOnPMUInterrupt = exit_sim_on_interrupt
                isa.pmu.addArchEvents(
                    cpu=cpu,
                    itb=cpu.mmu.itb,
                    dtb=cpu.mmu.dtb,
                    l2_shared=cpu.mmu.l2_shared,
                    icache=getattr(cpu, "icache", None),
                    dcache=getattr(cpu, "dcache", None),
                    l2cache=getattr(self, "l2", None),
                )
                for ev in events:
                    isa.pmu.addEvent(ev)

                isa.pmu.statCounters = isa.pmu.archStatCounters(*stat_counters)

    def connectMemSide(self, bus):
        try:
            self.l2.mem_side = bus.cpu_side_ports
        except AttributeError:
            for cpu in self.cpus:
                cpu.connectCachedPorts(bus.cpu_side_ports)

class ClusterSystem:
    """
    Base class providing cpu clusters generation/handling methods to
    SE/FS systems
    """

    def __init__(self, **kwargs):
        self._clusters = []

    def numCpuClusters(self):
        return len(self._clusters)

    def addCpuCluster(self, cpu_cluster):
        self._clusters.append(cpu_cluster)

    def addCaches(self, need_caches, last_cache_level):
        if not need_caches:
            # connect each cluster to the memory hierarchy
            for cluster in self._clusters:
                cluster.connectMemSide(self.membus)
            return

        cluster_mem_bus = self.membus
        assert last_cache_level >= 1 and last_cache_level <= 3
        for cluster in self._clusters:
            cluster.addL1()
        if last_cache_level > 1:
            for cluster in self._clusters:
                cluster.addL2(cluster.clk_domain)
        if last_cache_level > 2:
            max_clock_cluster = max(
                self._clusters, key=lambda c: c.clk_domain.clock[0]
            )
            self.l3 = L3(clk_domain=max_clock_cluster.clk_domain)
            self.toL3Bus = L2XBar(width=64)
            self.toL3Bus.mem_side_ports = self.l3.cpu_side
            self.l3.mem_side = self.membus.cpu_side_ports
            cluster_mem_bus = self.toL3Bus

        # connect each cluster to the memory hierarchy
        for cluster in self._clusters:
            cluster.connectMemSide(cluster_mem_bus)

class BaseSimpleSystem(ArmSystem, ClusterSystem):
    cache_line_size = 64

    def __init__(self, mem_size, platform, **kwargs):
        ArmSystem.__init__(self, **kwargs)
        ClusterSystem.__init__(self, **kwargs)

        self.voltage_domain = VoltageDomain(voltage="1.0V")
        self.clk_domain = SrcClockDomain(
            clock="1GHz", voltage_domain=Parent.voltage_domain
        )

        if platform is None:
            self.realview = VExpress_GEM5_V1()
        else:
            self.realview = platform

        if hasattr(self.realview.gic, "cpu_addr"):
            self.gic_cpu_addr = self.realview.gic.cpu_addr

        self.terminal = Terminal()
        self.vncserver = VncServer()

        self.iobus = IOXBar()
        # Device DMA -> MEM
        self.mem_ranges = self.getMemRanges(int(Addr(mem_size)))

    def getMemRanges(self, mem_size):
        """
        Define system memory ranges. This depends on the physical
        memory map provided by the realview platform and by the memory
        size provided by the user (mem_size argument).
        The method is iterating over all platform ranges until they cover
        the entire user's memory requirements.
        """
        mem_ranges = []
        for mem_range in self.realview._mem_regions:
            size_in_range = min(mem_size, mem_range.size())

            mem_ranges.append(
                AddrRange(start=mem_range.start, size=size_in_range)
            )

            mem_size -= size_in_range
            if mem_size == 0:
                return mem_ranges

        raise ValueError("memory size too big for platform capabilities")

        super().__init__(mem_size, platform, **kwargs)

        self.membus = MemBus()
        # CPUs->PIO

        self._caches = caches

    def connect(self):
        self.iobridge.mem_side_port = self.iobus.cpu_side_ports
        self.iobridge.cpu_side_port = self.membus.mem_side_ports

        if self._caches:

            self.iocache.cpu_side = self.iobus.mem_side_ports
        else:
            self.dmabridge.mem_side_port = self.membus.cpu_side_ports
            self.dmabridge.cpu_side_port = self.iobus.mem_side_ports

        if hasattr(self.realview.gic, "cpu_addr"):
            self.gic_cpu_addr = self.realview.gic.cpu_addr
        self.realview.attachOnChipIO(self.membus, self.iobridge)
        self.realview.attachIO(self.iobus)
        self.system_port = self.membus.cpu_side_ports

"""Create and configure the system object."""

    cpu_class = cpu_types[args.cpu][0]
    mem_mode = cpu_class.memory_mode()
    # Only simulate caches when using a timing CPU (e.g., the HPI model)
    want_caches = True if mem_mode == "timing" else False

    system = devices.SimpleSeSystem(
        mem_mode=mem_mode,
    )

    # Add CPUs to the system. A cluster of CPUs typically have
    # private L1 caches and a shared L2 cache.
    system.cpu_cluster = devices.ArmCpuCluster(
        system,
        args.num_cores,
        args.cpu_freq,
        "1.2V",
        *cpu_types[args.cpu],
        tarmac_gen=args.tarmac_gen,
        tarmac_dest=args.tarmac_dest,
    )

    # Create a cache hierarchy for the cluster. We are assuming that
    # clusters have core-private L1 caches and an L2 that's shared
    # within the cluster.
    system.addCaches(want_caches, last_cache_level=2)

    # Tell components about the expected physical memory ranges. This
    # is, for example, used by the MemConfig helper to determine where
    # to map DRAMs in the physical address space.
    system.mem_ranges = [AddrRange(start=0, size=args.mem_size)]

    # Configure the off-chip memory system.
    MemConfig.config_mem(args, system)

    # Wire up the system's memory system
    system.connect()

    # Parse the command line and get a list of Processes instances
    # that we can pass to gem5.
    processes = get_processes(args.commands_to_run)
    if len(processes) != args.num_cores:
        print(
            "Error: Cannot map %d command(s) onto %d CPU(s)"
            % (len(processes), args.num_cores)
        )
        sys.exit(1)

    system.workload = SEWorkload.init_compatible(processes[0].executable)

    def addL1(self):
        for cpu in self.cpus:
            l1i = None if self._l1i_type is None else self._l1i_type()
            l1d = None if self._l1d_type is None else self._l1d_type()
            cpu.addPrivateSplitL1Caches(l1i, l1d)

    def addL2(self, clk_domain):
        if self._l2_type is None:
            return
        self.toL2Bus = L2XBar(width=64, clk_domain=clk_domain)
        self.l2 = self._l2_type()
        for cpu in self.cpus:
            cpu.connectCachedPorts(self.toL2Bus.cpu_side_ports)
        self.toL2Bus.mem_side_ports = self.l2.cpu_side

    def addPMUs(
        self,
        ints,
        events=[],
        stat_counters=[],
        exit_sim_on_control=False,
        exit_sim_on_interrupt=False,
    ):
        """
        Instantiates 1 ArmPMU per PE. The method is accepting a list of
        interrupt numbers (ints) used by the PMU and a list of events to
        register in it.

        :param ints: List of interrupt numbers. The code will iterate over
            the cpu list in order and will assign to every cpu in the cluster
            a PMU with the matching interrupt.
        :type ints: List[int]
        :param events: Additional events to be measured by the PMUs
        :type events: List[Union[ProbeEvent, SoftwareIncrement]]
        :param exit_sim_on_control: If true, exit the sim loop when the PMU is
            enabled, disabled, or reset.
        :type exit_on_control: bool
        :param exit_sim_on_interrupt: If true, exit the sim loop when the PMU
            triggers an interrupt.
        :type exit_on_control: bool

        """
        # If ALL option has been passed, simply enable everything
        stat_counters = (
            EventTypeId.vals if "ALL" in stat_counters else stat_counters
        )

        assert len(ints) == len(self.cpus)
        for cpu, pint in zip(self.cpus, ints):
            int_cls = ArmPPI if pint < 32 else ArmSPI
            for isa in cpu.isa:
                isa.pmu = ArmPMU(interrupt=int_cls(num=pint))
                isa.pmu.exitOnPMUControl = exit_sim_on_control
                isa.pmu.exitOnPMUInterrupt = exit_sim_on_interrupt
                isa.pmu.addArchEvents(
                    cpu=cpu,
                    itb=cpu.mmu.itb,
                    dtb=cpu.mmu.dtb,
                    l2_shared=cpu.mmu.l2_shared,
                    icache=getattr(cpu, "icache", None),
                    dcache=getattr(cpu, "dcache", None),
                    l2cache=getattr(self, "l2", None),
                )
                for ev in events:
                    isa.pmu.addEvent(ev)

                isa.pmu.statCounters = isa.pmu.archStatCounters(*stat_counters)

    def connectMemSide(self, bus):
        try:
            self.l2.mem_side = bus.cpu_side_ports
        except AttributeError:
            for cpu in self.cpus:
                cpu.connectCachedPorts(bus.cpu_side_ports)
